heading: Publication

calibration.note: Same one-paper profile (14 proofs of arXiv 0708.2185); no new measurement was made for this problem. The rules are restated for a two-case proof with one auxiliary construction and one cited principle.

rules.rule: No sentence may be commentary only (placement inflight or leaf-section). A reason for a step may appear only as a clause of the sentence that takes the step.
No restatement of the claim before the derivation; the proof opens with its first step.

The boundary form of the maximum modulus principle is invoked in one sentence that says what it consumes (a polynomial, and a point of the closed unit disk) and what it returns. Compactness of the disk, which makes the supremum finite, is a clause and not a separate check.
At most 168 words; aim for 120 or fewer.
Every mandatory node of the content plan is realized or merged with an honest quote; every dependency between nodes in the alignment is still visible in the prose.

maximum-modulus-applicability.reason: PR3 requires the invoking sentence to say what the principle consumes, which is this question's answer.

circle-to-disk-transfer.reason: How a boundary bound reaches the interior is the content of the cited principle; a paper cites it and does not unfold it.

unit-disk-supremum-bound.reason: The defining bound of a supremum is used without justification beyond the compactness clause.
